stories.headline: Delhi High Court Refuses To Interfere With Centre's Decision To Close Kartarpur Corridor Following Pahalgam Terror Attack
stories.title: Delhi High Court Refuses To Interfere With Centre's Decision To Close Kartarpur Corridor Following Pahalgam Terror Attack
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'terror attack' in title weight 84
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday refused to entertain a plea seeking opening of the Kartarpur Corridor, a route connecting Gurdwara Dera Baba Nanak in Gurdaspur, Punjab, to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan.

A division bench comprising Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma noted that the decision was taken by the Government of India to close the corridor from May 07, 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack.
The plea was filed by NGO Paardarshita Public Welfare Foundation seeking opening of the corridor for Sikh pilgrims as they have great faith in the gurudwara in Kartarpur, Pakistan.

The Court said that the decision to close the corridor was taken by the government of India in the interest of the citizens and thus, in view of the policy decision, there was no reason to cause any interference in the same in extraordinary writ jurisdiction.
However, noting that the representation of the petitioner was pending with the authorities, the Court said that it trusts and hopes that the respondents shall look into the same.
“With the aforesaid liberty, the petition stands disposed of,” the Court said.

stories.headline: Accessment of flood damages: High level Inter Ministerial team arrives in JK, to visit multiple flood hit districts
stories.title: Accessment of flood damages: High level Inter Ministerial team arrives in JK, to visit multiple flood hit districts
stories.summary: Rajouri, Nov 25: For on spot accessment of the situation after flash floods, a high level Inter Ministerial team from Government of India has arrived in Jammu and Kashmir which will visit multiple flood hit districts in next two days. The team is headed by a Joint Secretary (F-II) ranked officer of Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India and is comprising of officers from other Ministeries including Ministry of Roads, Transport and Highways, Power Department, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Jal Shakti Department and Department of Space, GoI. Official sources said that the team will be split in two sub-teams with one team will be deputed to districts of Chenab valley including Doda and Kishtwar while another team will be visiting Rajouri and Poonch districts. The sub-team deputed to Rajouri and Poonch has already arrived in Rajouri district with senior officers of district administration are accompanying the team which is scheduled to visit various flood hit areas where devastation in floods happened in this year's flood. Official sources stated that the team will examine post flood situation after which it will submit a detailed report before Government of India based on which financial packages will be sanctioned. Earlier, on Tuesday, during visit of Rajouri, Chief Secretary Dr. Sajjan Singh Yadav also told media persons that a high level inter-ministerial team is visiting areas of Jammu and Kashmir. " Central team is visiting Jammu and Kashmir tomorrow which will conduct visit of flood hit areas after which financial package will be given to us by which we will be able to compensate the losses of victims and will also pace up rebuilding of necessary infrastructure." CS had said.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(November 25) issued notice to the Delhi police on bail pleas of Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 Delhi riots larger conspiracy case under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act after the Delhi High Court denied them bail recently.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana however, declined to consider their plea for interim bail today.
Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal, for Khalid, pressed for interim bail, saying that he had been under custody for over six years.
Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave raised a similar plea for Sharjeel Imam.
The bench however said that it will hear the respondent before considering the interim prayer.

The bench directed that the matters be put up before the Chief Justice of India on the administrative side for the constitution of a 3-judge bench in the light of the reference order passed by a two-judge bench on May 22 this year in Tasleem Ahmed regarding the perceived conflict between the judgment in Gulfisha Fatima (which denied bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in January 2026) and the KA Najeeb judgment (which held that long incarceration and delay in trial can be grounds for bail regardless of the stringent conditions under the UAPA).
Sibal then pointed out that in Tasleem Ahmed, the bench had granted interim bail to co-accused in the riots conspiracy while passing the reference order.
"Not today," CJI replied swiftly.
"You have made a prayer for interim relief; let it be responded," Justice Bagchi said.
The CJI said that a 3-judge bench has to be constituted to hear the issue.

Dave, however said that the reference order has no bearing on the present petitions, as they are filed pursuant to the earlier judgment of January, which allowed them to apply for bail after one year.
Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta, for the Delhi.

stories.title: Supreme Court sets aside HC order for CBI, ED probe into Rahul Gandhi's assets

article_sentences: The Supreme Court set aside Allahabad High Court orders directing the CBI and ED to verify allegations that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi possesses disproportionate assets and remitted the matter to the High Court for fresh consideration.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside Allahabad High Court orders directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to verify allegations that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi possesses assets disproportionate to his known sources of income.
A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant remitted the matter to the Allahabad High Court for fresh consideration.
The High Court had earlier directed the central agencies to verify the allegations raised by Karnataka-based BJP worker Vignesh Shishir and apprise it of the progress made on his complaint.
Rahul Gandhi had approached the Supreme Court challenging the Allahabad High Court's orders in the case concerning allegations that he holds assets disproportionate to his income.
In an order passed in May, the Allahabad High Court directed that the allegations in the complaint against the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha be verified in accordance with the law.
The High Court had observed that if the complaint had been received, the allegations could be verified as per law.
It had also said that the CBI or ED could take appropriate steps permissible under the law.
"It is expected that if the complaint of the petitioner has been received, the allegations of the complaints may be verified as per law.
It is needless to say that the CBI or ED may take appropriate steps which are permissible under the law," the High Court had said.
The court subsequently directed the agencies to apprise it of the progress made in the matter.
In a subsequent order dated July 20, the High Court expressed dissatisfaction with the affidavit filed by the CBI, observing that it was not in accordance with its earlier direction.

The Collegium has also recommended the transfer of Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court, as the Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court.
The recommendations were made at a Collegium meeting held on November 24, 2026.
Justice Bakhru's transfer to the Jharkhand High Court is consequent upon the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice of the High Court on November 27, 2026.
Justice Bakhru was elevated as a judge of the Delhi High Court in 2013.

Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, who hails from the Telangana High Court, was appointed as the Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court.
He has previously served as a judge of the Telangana and Andhra Pradesh High Courts.

stories.headline: Days before Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice’s retirement, Supreme Court Collegium proposes successor
stories.title: Days before Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice’s retirement, Supreme Court Collegium proposes successor
stories.summary: The Collegium’s decision has come shortly after Chief Minister Hemant Soren wrote to Chief Justice of India, expressing concern about a lack of decision regarding a successor to Justice Sonak, superannuating on November 27
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

event term: 'chief justice of india' in summary weight 27.6
article_sentences: Hardly three days before the retirement of incumbent Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M.S. Sonak, the Supreme Court Collegium headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) proposed the transfer of Karnataka High Court Chief Vibhu Bakhru to the office.

The Collegium’s decision has come shortly after Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Sorenwrote to the Chief Justice of India, expressing concern about a lack of decision regarding a successor to Justice Sonak, who is superannuating on November 27.

Mr. Soren had highlighted that a Chief Justice to the State High Court should ideally have been recommended by the Supreme Court Collegium in advance, and cleared by the Union government as per the Memorandum of Procedure for appointment of judges to the constitutional courts.

The Chief Minister, as the head of the State government had expressed objections about any interim arrangement, making it clear that the State High Court must have a regular Chief Justice at the helm.

Mr. Soren, in his letter to the CJI and the Collegium judges, had reportedly pointed out that frequent transitions accompanied by extended interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affect institutional planning and create uncertainty within the judicial establishment.
On Tuesday (November 24), the Supreme Court Collegium proposed that Justice Bakhru take over as Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court upon the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice.
The ball is now with the government to clear the Collegium resolution and notify the appointment of Justice Bakhru by November 27.
The Collegium has recommended Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, the Chief Justice of Tripura High Court, to be transferred as the Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court in the place of Justice Bakhru.

In a separate resolution on November 24, the Collegium recommended the appointment of Himachal Pradesh High Court judge, Justice Vivek Singh Thakur, as Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court following the transfer of Justice Rao to Karnataka High Court.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea Challenging Exclusion Of Released Women Officers From Indian Coast Guard Permanent Absorption
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea Challenging Exclusion Of Released Women Officers From Indian Coast Guard Permanent Absorption
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently issued notice on the plea filed by a woman Indian Coast Guard officer, released from service, challenging the ICG policy which allowed SSA women officers of the General Duty branch to opt for Permanent Appointment.

The policy is contested on the ground that it unfairly limits the option to officers "in service as on date", excluding officers like the petitioner who were released on completion of the maximum SSA engagement (14 years) before the policy was issued.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the order, issuing notice to the Union and Director General of ICG.

Advocates Siddhant Sharma, Prafull Bhardwaj and Snehil Himanshi appeared for the petitioner, ex-commandant (JG) Priyanka, who served in the Coast Guard for 14 years before being released in December 2023.
Briefly put, the petition challenges policy letters dated 18.08.2026, which for the first time allowed women SSA officers of the General Duty branch to opt for permanent appointment.
As per claims, the petitioner joined the Coast Guard on 30.12.2009 as part of the pioneer SSA (GD) course.
In March 2023, she formally made a request for permanent absorption.
Her request was recommended at every level in the chain of command, with superiors suggesting a policy change if needed.
However no decision was conveyed before her release in 2023.

The petition refers to an eligible officer (Priyanka Tyagi) under the new policy who hails from the same batch as the petitioner (December 2009), underlining that she was also released from service in 2023 but continues in service as on date because of Supreme Court's interim order [Ref: Priyanka Tyagi.
Union of India].
It is also claimed that 11 out of 36 eligible officers listed in the petition had crossed 14 years of service before the impugned policy was issued.

stories.headline: NSA Doval calls for closer regional security cooperation to counter challenges in Indian Ocean
stories.title: NSA Doval calls for closer regional security cooperation to counter challenges in Indian Ocean
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 25: India remains committed to working closely with key Indian Ocean nations to enhance their collective capacities to deal with evolving security threats, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval said on Wednesday. In his address at the eighth Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) in Male, Doval listed various pressing challenges facing the region and called for deeper strategic cooperation to address them. The CSC has emerged as a key regional security grouping of Indian Ocean littoral states, comprising India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh, and Seychelles. It has largely been focusing on maritime safety, counter-terrorism, and transnational security cooperation. "The Colombo Security Conclave represents the intersection of our Neighborhood First outlook and the MAHASAGAR vision," Doval said. "We are committed to continue working closely with the CSC countries to enhance our collective capacities in dealing with the evolving serious security challenges," he added. Last March, during his visit to Mauritius, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the vision MAHASAGAR, or 'Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions, for India's engagement with the Global South. Doval said he was confident that the CSC will become an effective instrument in the Indian Ocean region to provide collective security and look after common interests. "India has been trying to work very closely with Sri Lanka, with the Maldives and other countries, and we want to see that this cooperation is further extended," the NSA said. "I assure all of you that India, as one of the countries which had initiated the idea of the Colombo Security Conclave, will give its best and will try to give all necessary help, assistance. I assure you of our fullest commitment to achieve our common objectives," Doval added. The Colombo Security Conclave was established in 2020 when India, Sri Lanka and Maldives agreed to expand the scope and membership of their trilateral meeting on maritime cooperation. Cooperation under the CSC focuses on the five pillars of maritime safety and security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, combating trafficking and transnational organised crime and cyber security, protection of critical infrastructure, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.

stories.title: Amazon's e-commerce exports from India reach $27 bn; number of exporters jump 20% in a year
stories.summary: Delhi with 36,000 exporters tops the Amazon Global Selling programme, followed by Rajasthan (over 32,500), UP (over 29,000), Gujarat (over 28,000) and Maharashtra (over 23,500)
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: E-commerce major Amazon on Wednesday said it has reached $27 billion in cumulative exports from India through its Amazon Global Selling programme, with the number of exporters on the platform rising 20 per cent in a year to 2.4 lakh.
The milestone marks progress towards Amazon's goal of enabling $80 billion in cumulative e-commerce exports from India by 2030, the company said in a statement.
Launched in 2015, the programme has enabled the sale of more than one billion 'Made-in-India' products to customers across Amazon's global marketplaces.
Among smaller cities, exporters from Erode in Tamil Nadu crossed $121.5 million in sales between January 2025 and the third quarter of 2026.

Health and personal care (45 per cent), groceries (44 per cent), beauty (42 per cent) and toys (35 per cent) emerged as the top-performing categories, recording the highest compound annual growth rates (CAGR) over the last 10 years, the company said.

stories.headline: IMD update: TN, Kerala to stay wet as easterly wave keeps South Peninsula on rainy track
stories.title: IMD update: TN, Kerala to stay wet as easterly wave keeps South Peninsula on rainy track
stories.summary: An easterly wave is a weather disturbance embedded in easterly winds headed towards Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu coast promoting conditions that encourage air to rise, cool and condense into rain clouds
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The South Peninsula remains in the grip of rain-bearing easterly disturbances, with isolated heavy rainfall likely over Kerala and Mahe, and Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, for three days from Wednesday.

Strong surface winds are also expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam, and Rayalaseema, as a combination of easterly waves, atmospheric troughs and cyclonic circulations sustains unsettled weather across the region.
The wave is a westward-moving disturbance embedded in the easterly winds over the Bay of Bengal.

As it travels towards Sri Lanka and the Tamil Nadu coast, it carries enhanced cyclonic vorticity and a zone of atmospheric convergence, or conditions that encourage air to rise, cool and condense into rain-bearing clouds.
Its passage can also reinforce existing troughs and strengthen wind convergence, cloud development and rainfall.
Showers generally occur along and behind the wave trough, while sinking air ahead of it tends to favour relatively fairer or drier weather.
The latest spell brought heavy rain to isolated places over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on Tuesday.
In the 12 hours ending at 5.30 am on Wednesday, Karaikal recorded 5 cm of rainfall, while Nellore and Ongole in Andhra Pradesh, and Bengaluru HAL in Karnataka, received 3 cm each.
The atmospheric setting remains favourable for further rainfall.

Two troughs in the easterlies, one extending from the south-west Bay of Bengal to the west-central Bay, and another from the Comorin area to Rayalaseema across interior Tamil Nadu, persisted into Wednesday morning.
A cyclonic circulation was also located over south Kerala.

Acting in tandem with the prevailing easterly wave, these systems can sustain moisture convergence, rising air and cloud formation, keeping much of the South Peninsula vulnerable to further spells of rain.
